messages.subject: Dumb GRM question
parts:
This may be a dumb question, but I'd really appreciate having someone check my thinking.

The graded response model in item response theory is formulated as P(y_ij)<=k)=invlogit(ability_jk-discrimination_j*difficulty_i) (for i questions, j, students, and k ordered options per question, and thus k-1 ability parameters per question, representing cutpoints in a latent ability variable). I'd like to model this using the ordered_logistic (ordered_logistic_log, strictly) function, which is parameterized in terms of invlogit(eta-c_k).

1) Am I right that c corresponds to ability, so that the ordered_logistic call would be something of the form ordered_logistic(discrimination[k[i]]*difficulty[k[i]],ability[j[i])?

2) Am I right that this would result in parameter estimates with the wrong signs (since I want c_k-eta, which is -1*(eta-c_k)?

I've been beating myself up for not being able to get the same results with my stan model as I get from basic grm software in R, and am realizing I may have misinterpreted something in using ordered_logistic, and really appreciate any tips you all could share.

Thanks,
Josh

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] GRM question
parts:
There are a lot of different ways to parameterize the
ordered logistic --- Gelman and Hill cover quite a few.
Stan just chose one.

You can also just bypass Stan's ordered logistic and define
your own. For example, the ordered logistic we built in
could be defined by setting a parameter vector theta to the
probabilities of outcome k in the definition and then sampling
from a categorical with that parameter set.

On 11/1/13, 8:30 PM, Joshua Rosenau wrote:
> This may be a dumb question, but I'd really appreciate having someone check my thinking.
>
> The graded response model in item response theory is formulated as
> P(y_ij)<=k)=invlogit(ability_jk-discrimination_j*difficulty_i) (for i questions, j, students, and k
> ordered options per question, and thus k-1 ability parameters per question,
> representing cutpoints in a latent ability variable).

I don't know the GRM, but the IRT models I have seen are
of the form

discriminiation_i * (ability_j - difficulty_i)

or

(discrimation_i * ability_j) - difficulty_i

where i is the index for questions and j the index for students.

My understanding seems to be in line with the first hit on my search:

http://www.ub.edu/gdne/documents/IRT_gradedresponsemodel.pdf

Which R package and function are you using and does it have
a definition somewhere of what it's doing?
> I'd like to model this using the ordered_logistic (ordered_logistic_log, strictly)

It's "ordered_logistic" in a sampling statement and "ordered_logistic_log" as
a function.
> function, which is parameterized in terms of invlogit(eta-c_k).

eta is the linear predictor and c_k is the cutpoint. It helps
to look at the boundary, where with K outcomes, the probability
of the highest outcome K is:

OrderedLogistic(K | eta, c) = inv_logit(eta - c[K-1])

and the chance of the lowest is:

OrdereLogistic(1 | eta, c) = 1 - inv_logit(eta - c[1])

So as eta goes up, the chance of the highest grade (K) goes up and
the chance of the lowest grade (1) goes down.

> 1) Am I right that c corresponds to ability,
> so that the ordered_logistic call would be something
> of the form ordered_logistic(discrimination[k[i]]*difficulty[k[i]],ability[j[i])?

There's no intrinsic correspondence to ability or anything in the
ordered_logistic. I hope the above explanation of the role of eta and
c helps.

> 2) Am I right that this would result in parameter estimates with the
> wrong signs (since I want c_k-eta, which is -1*(eta-c_k)?

If it turns out you really want c_k - eta, you will probably need to write
your own distribution. Maybe not if everything just reverses. The key
relation is

inv_logit(-a) = 1 - inv_logit(a)

- Bob

messages.author: 6b3b475e6af83898
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] GRM question
parts:
Thanks, and infinite apologies for having mixed up the parameters in writing the email. It's right in my stan code, but I thoughtlessly transposed some items in writing the email.

On reflection, though, I realize that the difficulty parameter, not the ability parameter, is broken up across cut points (so an item on a 5-point Likert scale has 4 difficulty parameters, but the person answering that item shouldn't have 4 ability parameters!). The GRM is specified by:

P(y_ij)<=k)=invlogit(discrimination_i*ability_j-difficulty_ik) (for i questions, j, students, and k ordered options per question, and thus k-1 difficulty parameters per question, representing cutpoints in a latent difficulty variable).

Thus, it seems like I should be able to set ordered_logistic()'s theta to discrimination[i]*ability[j] and let c be difficulty[i[n]][k[n]], yielding the call: ordered_logistic(discrimination[k]*ability[j],difficulty[k])

Right? That also renders my second question superfluous.

In the end, I think I'll still need to roll my own ordered logistic to extend this model to multiple dimensions, etc., but I'd like to build it in pieces, and to be certain I'm understanding what stan's doing along the way.

Many thanks,
Josh
